summary: Delivery review for iteration `welcome-email` is blocked by build verification in this environment. Source review found the implementation aligned with the iteration objective: Gmail config is read server-side from `GMAIL_USER`, `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD`, and `GMAIL_FROM`; welcome sending is server-only and injectable; Auth.js triggers delivery from `events.createUser` after persisted user creation; existing-user sign-in does not call the delivery path; `welcomeEmailAttemptedAt` claims a single attempt to avoid duplicates; failures are caught and logged without obvious secret fields. Successful checks run in this review: `npm.cmd ls next next-auth @auth/prisma-adapter @prisma/client prisma typescript --depth=0`; `npx.cmd prisma validate`; `npx.cmd tsc --noEmit --incremental false`; `node --test .ai_factory\tests\unit\registration\registration-profile-consent-source.test.mjs .ai_factory\tests\unit\registration\welcome-email-source.test.mjs` with 9/9 passing; and `npm.cmd run lint`. Blocker evidence: `npm.cmd run build` printed `> customer-feedback-portal@0.1.0 build`, `> next build`, the Next.js 15.5.25 banner, and `- Environments: .env.local`, then remained active with no further output across multiple 30-second wait windows; it was stopped with Ctrl+C and exited code 1. Browser verification, Playwright, app server startup, deployment, publishing, and real Gmail delivery were not run per task constraints and are not claimed as passed.
